title: Windows GPU unit tests job fails extracting OpenVINO packages due to locked tbb12.dll
signature: windows runner extract openvino packages expand-archive remove-item access to the path denied unauthorizedaccessexception locked dll file|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step fails: Remove-Item cannot delete tbb12.dll - Access to the path is denied

key_errors:
Remove-Item : Cannot remove item C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll:
Access to the path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll' is denied.
At C:\Windows\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive.psm1:1029
+ FullyQualifiedErrorId : RemoveFileSystemItemUnAuthorizedAccess,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.RemoveItemCommand
root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs Expand-Archive -Force on openvino_package.zip and openvino_tests.zip into the shared install directory. PowerShell's Expand-Archive with -Force first tries to delete pre-existing files at the destination before overwriting them. tbb12.dll under install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin was still locked (loaded by another process, e.g. an antivirus scan, an unreleased handle from a previous step, or a lingering test/runner process on the self-hosted Windows runner) when Remove-Item attempted to delete it, raising UnauthorizedAccessException and aborting the archive extraction with exit code 1. This is a transient runner/environment resource-locking issue rather than a code defect.
reproduction_steps: Not directly reproducible locally; this depends on Windows self-hosted runner state. To reproduce the failure mode: on a Windows machine, load tbb12.dll into a running process (e.g. via a lingering test binary), then run Expand-Archive -Force targeting a destination containing that locked file - Remove-Item will fail with UnauthorizedAccessException.
recommended_actions: Ensure the install directory is fully cleaned (and any processes holding handles to it, e.g. leftover test executables or antivirus scanners, are terminated/excluded) before the 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs.
Consider extracting to a fresh/unique directory per run instead of overwriting an existing install directory with -Force, avoiding delete-before-overwrite races entirely.
Add a retry-with-backoff wrapper around the Expand-Archive step for Windows jobs, since file-lock contention on shared runner directories is often transient.
Investigate whether a prior step (build, packaging, or a previous test job on the same runner) leaves tbb12.dll loaded/locked and add an explicit cleanup/wait step.
prevention_strategies: Isolate extraction destinations per job/run to prevent overwrite-induced delete races; add file-lock-aware retry logic around PowerShell Expand-Archive/Remove-Item calls on Windows runners; audit self-hosted Windows runner hygiene (stale processes, antivirus real-time scanning of install directories) that can hold file handles open between jobs.
historical_context: No prior post-commit investigations in the knowledge base matched this exact signature (tbb12.dll lock during Expand-Archive). Related but distinct Windows infrastructure patterns previously recorded include: Windows CC build out-of-memory errors under high parallelism, Windows build jobs terminated mid-build with unavailable logs, and pip-proxy malformed JSON responses breaking Windows dependency installs - all pointing to broader self-hosted Windows runner instability.
